reports.rendered_content: The algorithm implementation now includes a real coverage engine with 17 new files, supporting both fixed-first and genuine joint-pair search modes. Joint mode evaluates all legal coarse pairs ranked by bitset union before applying quality tie-breakers, avoiding premature discard of complementary origins. The surface sampler is deterministic, sampling triangles proportional to world-space area. Origin evaluation includes segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, and separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets. However, the implementation has critical blockers: (1) imported sets using whole-object AABBs as obstacles cause zero clearance for origins inside large bounding boxes (e.g., room shells or combined furniture), rejecting all sensible camera positions; fix requires actual geometry clearance via triangle-level collision checks or per-mesh spatial clustering rather than per-imported-set AABBs; (2) the triangle-expansion-based geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports. Readiness for complex imported sets remains low (4/10), though the core math/search design is mostly correct (8/10 overall architecture).
